title: Have Gun, Will Travel
paragraphs: The radio version of the Western follows Paladin, a sophisticated San Francisco-based gunfighter who hires out his skills but often relies on judgment and negotiation as much as a weapon.
CBS radio Western adapted from the earlier television property, starring John Dehner as Paladin.

The run breaks into several distinct periods: TV-script adaptation era (November 23, 1958 to August 16, 1959) on [[org|org.8480b75bc0c36e4b|CBS Radio Network]] and Original radio-plot era (August 23, 1959 to November 27, 1960) on [[org|org.8480b75bc0c36e4b|CBS Radio Network]].

Names that turn up again and again in the surviving run include [[person|john-dehner|John Dehner]] (performer), Herb Meadow (creator, writer, and performer), Sam Rolfe (creator and writer), Ben Wright (performer), Hugh Douglas (announcer and performer), Bill James (sound-effects artist), and Tom Hanley (sound-effects artist, writer, and performer).
Across its run, the surviving broadcasts are tied to [[org|org.8480b75bc0c36e4b|CBS Radio Network]] and [[org|org.cd82fd99edb39caa|Armed Forces Radio and Television Service]].

The stories often return to justice and moral judgment, hired gun and professional assignment, outlaws and violent crime, ranches and frontier property, Native American frontier conflict, and railroads and stage travel.
The show also sits in a wider radio history that includes Television-to-radio adaptation, Late network radio drama, and Adult Western storytelling.

If you are following the same actors and creative circles, related programs worth opening next include [[show|gunsmoke|Gunsmoke]], [[show|yours-truly-johnny-dollar|Yours Truly, Johnny Dollar]], [[show|lux-radio-theatre|Lux Radio Theatre]], [[show|escape|Escape]], and [[show|cbs-radio-workshop|CBS Radio Workshop]].

CBS radio Western adapted from the earlier television property, starring John Dehner as Paladin.

Across its run, the surviving broadcasts are tied to CBS Radio Network and Armed Forces Radio and Television Service.

The stories often return to justice and moral judgment, hired gun and professional assignment, outlaws and violent crime, ranches and frontier property, Native American frontier conflict, and railroads and stage travel.

The show also sits in a wider radio history that includes Television-to-radio adaptation, Late network radio drama, and Adult Western storytelling.
